label: Land-neighbor ruler incl. tributaries
summary: Each ruler whose realm touches the realm of the character's top liege by land, counting tributary borders.
details: A realm with a different top liege (the ruler at the very top of the feudal chain) counts, and the list gives you that realm's holder. Borders extended through tributaries (rulers who pay a suzerain) count too. The game says the borders can be a day or two out of date. Vanilla uses it to collect possible opponents and to find the strongest neighbours.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the neighbours that pass these checks.

fields.name: order_by
fields.text: Only for the ordered form: the value used to rank the neighbours.

fields.name: position
fields.text: Only for the ordered form: which rank to pick, starting at 0.

label: Learning councillor
summary: Each councillor of the character whose council task is based on the learning skill.
details: The items are characters. Vanilla uses it to add opinions to them (one use gives them an opinion of the current character) and to save one as the court chaplain or priest, or to look for one with a high learning skill.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the councillors that pass these checks.

label: Leased title
summary: Each title that is leased to the holy order.
details: Works on a holy order. The items are titles. Vanilla uses it to notify the holders of leased counties and to find a monastery that was taken from an order.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the titles that pass these checks.

label: Legend
summary: Every legend in the world that has not been completed yet.
details: Needs no starting object, it looks at the whole world. The items are legends. Vanilla uses it to pick a legend to promote and to check which legends a character could become the owner of.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the legends that pass these checks.

label: Legend promoter
summary: Each character who promotes the legend.
details: Works on a legend. The items are characters. Vanilla mostly checks whether the current character is one of them.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the promoters that pass these checks.

label: Legend type
summary: Every legend type defined in the game.
details: These are the kinds of legend the game knows, not legends that exist in a game. Needs no starting object. Vanilla does not use it.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the legend types that pass these checks.

label: Liege or above
summary: Each liege above the character, from their own liege up to the top, without the character themselves.
details: Works on a character. The items are characters. Vanilla uses it to inform lieges by event or message, to give them opinions, and to test whether any liege above is at war, of a given faith, or a human player.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the lieges that pass these checks.

fields.name: order_by
fields.text: Only for the ordered form: the value used to rank the lieges.
fields.values: a script value, for example highest_held_title_tier

fields.name: position
fields.text: Only for the ordered form: which rank to pick, starting at 0.

label: Random list
summary: Picks one entry out of a weighted set of outcomes and runs it.
details: This is not a loop over game objects. Each entry starts with a number, its weight: the higher the number, the likelier the entry. An entry can have a `trigger` that switches it on or off, and a modifier block that changes its chance. Vanilla uses it heavily in events, with weights such as 1, 10, 20 or 50. Entries can be empty (for example `75 = {}`), so one can mean nothing happens.

fields.name: pick
fields.text: How many entries to pick instead of just one. The game's documentation does not mention it; vanilla writes it in a few lists, mostly as 1 and sometimes 2 or 3.

fields.name: unique
fields.text: Vanilla writes it as `yes` together with pick, which suggests the same entry is not drawn twice (inferred, the game's documentation does not say).

fields.name: desc
fields.text: A text key that vanilla puts in the list block; going by its use, it is a description shown for the list in tooltips (inferred, the game's documentation does not say).

label: Living character
summary: Every character in the world who is alive.
details: Needs no starting object. The items are characters. It covers the whole world, so use a limit to narrow it. Vanilla uses it to pick random characters for portraits.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the characters that pass these checks.

label: Log scopes
summary: A debugging aid that writes the current object to the game's random log when it runs.
details: `yes` logs the full information about the object, `no` only the current object. The game warns to use it only for a short time, because it can put localized strings into the log. It is not a loop and has no items. Vanilla uses it once, with `yes`.

label: Men-at-arms regiment
summary: Each men-at-arms regiment of the character.
details: Works on a character. The items are regiments. Vanilla uses it to change a regiment's size or troop count, to destroy it, to move a title regiment to another title, and to test its type or how full it is.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the regiments that pass these checks.

fields.name: order_by
fields.text: Only for the ordered form: the value used to rank the regiments.
fields.values: a script value, for example maa_size

fields.name: position
fields.text: Only for the ordered form: which rank to pick, starting at 0.

label: Martial councillor
summary: Each councillor of the character whose council task is based on the martial skill.
details: The items are characters. Vanilla uses it to find the marshal and to test the martial skill of a councillor.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the councillors that pass these checks.

label: Memory
summary: Each memory the character has.
details: Works on a character. The items are memories. You can write a memory type directly in the block to keep only memories of that type. Vanilla often ranks them by `memory_creation_date` to find the newest or oldest.

fields.name: memory_type
fields.text: Keeps only memories of this type.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the memories that pass these checks.

fields.name: order_by
fields.text: Only for the ordered form: the value used to rank the memories.
fields.values: a script value, for example memory_creation_date

label: Memory participant
summary: Each character who took part in the memory.
details: Works on a memory. The items are characters. Vanilla uses it to find a particular person in a memory, such as a sex partner or a king, to keep one other than the current character, and to check family ties or whether they are alive.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the participants that pass these checks.

label: Mercenary company
summary: Every mercenary company in the world.
details: Needs no starting object. The items are mercenary companies. Vanilla uses it only a little, to look at the company's leader and to test whether a company is in hire range of someone.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the companies that pass these checks.

label: Neighboring or overseas realm owner
summary: Each ruler of a realm or sub-realm that borders the character's realm, including across water.
details: The items are characters. The game's documentation says it returns "counts and above", most likely meaning counties and above, so rulers of county rank or higher. Vanilla uses it little.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the rulers that pass these checks.

label: Same-rank neighbor or overseas
summary: Each ruler of a realm bordering the character's realm, including across water, who has the same rank as the character.
details: The items are characters. If needed, the game looks up the liege chain of the land's owner to find a ruler of that rank. Vanilla uses it to find possible helpers, targets and candidates, and to check for neighbours with stealable ships or who could be converted.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the rulers that pass these checks.

label: Neighboring or overseas top realm
summary: Each realm with a different top liege that borders the realm of the character's top liege, including across water, as its top title.
details: The items are titles, not characters. Use `holder` to reach the ruler. Borders can be a day or two out of date. Vanilla uses it to pick a border realm and to save it for later.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the realms that pass these checks.

label: Neighboring or overseas top liege
summary: Each ruler of a realm with a different top liege that borders the realm of the character's top liege, including across water.
details: Same as the top realm list, but the items are the rulers (characters). Borders can be a day or two out of date. Vanilla uses it a lot, to fill lists of targets, to rank neighbours by military strength or opinion, and to test properties of neighbours.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the rulers that pass these checks.

fields.name: order_by
fields.text: Only for the ordered form: the value used to rank the rulers.
fields.values: a script value, for example current_military_strength

fields.name: position
fields.text: Only for the ordered form: which rank to pick, starting at 0.

label: Neighboring or overseas top suzerain realm
summary: Each realm with a different top suzerain that borders the realm of the character's top suzerain, including across water, as its top title.
details: A suzerain is the overlord that a tributary pays. The items are titles, not characters. Borders can be a day or two out of date. Vanilla does not use it.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the realms that pass these checks.

label: Neighboring or overseas top suzerain
summary: Each ruler of a realm with a different top suzerain that borders the realm of the character's top suzerain, including across water.
details: Like the top suzerain realm list, but the items are the rulers (characters). Borders can be a day or two out of date. Vanilla does not use it.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the rulers that pass these checks.

label: Neighboring county
summary: Each county that borders the current county.
details: Only works on a county. The items are counties. Vanilla uses it to spread modifiers, faith or culture to the neighbours, to collect lists of counties, and to test the holder or faith of the neighbours.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the counties that pass these checks.

fields.name: order_by
fields.text: Only for the ordered form: the value used to rank the counties.

label: Neighboring faith
summary: Each faith that has a county bordering a county of the current faith.
details: Works on a faith. The items are faiths. The game warns that it can be expensive, so use it with care. Vanilla uses it once, to pick a faith to learn from.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the faiths that pass these checks.

label: Neighboring province
summary: Each province that borders the current province.
details: Works on a province. The items are provinces. Vanilla also tests sea provinces inside it, so they appear to be included. Vanilla uses it to pick a neighbouring county or a sea province, to find coastal or river provinces, and to apply province modifiers with a chance to each neighbour.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the provinces that pass these checks.

label: Neighboring realm owner
summary: Each ruler of a realm or sub-realm that borders the character's realm.
details: The items are characters. The game's documentation says it returns "counts and above", most likely meaning counties and above, so rulers of county rank or higher. The game's documentation does not mention water, unlike the "across water" variant, so crossings over water are presumably not included. Vanilla does not use it.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the rulers that pass these checks.

label: Same-rank neighboring realm owner
summary: Each ruler of a realm bordering the character's realm who has the same rank as the character.
details: The items are characters. If needed, the game looks up the liege chain of the land's owner to find a ruler of that rank. Vanilla uses it to find neighbouring rulers for tasks and events, to add opinions, and to rank them by land fertility.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the rulers that pass these checks.

fields.name: order_by
fields.text: Only for the ordered form: the value used to rank the rulers.

label: Neighbor ruler incl. tributaries
summary: Each ruler whose realm borders the realm of the character's top liege, counting land and water borders extended through tributaries.
details: A realm with a different top liege counts, and the list gives you its holder. Tributaries (rulers who pay a suzerain) widen the borders. Borders can be a day or two out of date. Vanilla uses it once, to exclude a particular character.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the rulers that pass these checks.

label: Neighboring top realm
summary: Each realm with a different top liege that borders the realm of the character's top liege, as its top title.
details: The items are titles, not characters. Use `holder` to reach the ruler. Borders can be a day or two out of date, and water crossings are not included. Vanilla uses it to pick a neighbouring realm and to test its holder.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the realms that pass these checks.

label: Neighboring top liege
summary: Each ruler of a realm with a different top liege that borders the realm of the character's top liege.
details: Like the top realm list, but the items are the rulers (characters). Borders can be a day or two out of date, and water crossings are not included. Vanilla uses it a lot, to fill target lists, to rank neighbours by opinion or strength, and to test their title, faith or government.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the rulers that pass these checks.

fields.name: order_by
fields.text: Only for the ordered form: the value used to rank the rulers.
fields.values: a script value, for example current_military_strength

fields.name: position
fields.text: Only for the ordered form: which rank to pick, starting at 0.

label: Neighboring top suzerain realm
summary: Each realm with a different top suzerain that borders the realm of the character's top suzerain, as its top title.
details: A suzerain is the overlord that a tributary pays. The items are titles, not characters. Borders can be a day or two out of date. Vanilla does not use it.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the realms that pass these checks.

label: Neighboring top suzerain
summary: Each ruler of a realm with a different top suzerain that borders the realm of the character's top suzerain.
details: Like the top suzerain realm list, but the items are the rulers (characters). Borders can be a day or two out of date. Vanilla uses it once, to exclude one character.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the rulers that pass these checks.

label: Noble family title
summary: Each noble family title in the realm of the character.
details: The items are titles. If the character is not independent, the list is empty. Vanilla uses it to remove a variable from each title's holder and to set each title's coat of arms from its holder's house.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the titles that pass these checks.

label: Open-invite activity
summary: Every activity in the world that is open for anyone to be invited to.
details: Needs no starting object. The items are activities. Vanilla uses it once, to look for a tournament that a character could join.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the activities that pass these checks.

label: Opposite-sex spouse candidate
summary: Each character of the opposite sex who is a possible spouse for the character.
details: The items are characters. The game warns that it is very slow, so do not use it often. Vanilla does not use it.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the candidates that pass these checks.

label: Opposite trait
summary: Each trait that is the opposite of the current trait.
details: Works on a trait. The items are traits. Vanilla uses it to check whether a character has the opposite of a trait, or to remove it.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the traits that pass these checks.

label: Organization member
summary: Each member of the organization.
details: Works on an organization. The items are characters. Vanilla uses it twice, to run an effect for the clergy and to test members for a faith claim.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the members that pass these checks.

label: Story
summary: Each story the character owns.
details: Works on a character. The items are stories, the long-running story cycles such as a pet. You can name a story type to keep only stories of that type. Vanilla uses it to end stories and to read or change their variables.

fields.name: type
fields.text: Keeps only stories of this type.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the stories that pass these checks.

label: Owned title regiment
summary: Each men-at-arms regiment that is owned by the title.
details: Works on a title. The items are regiments. Vanilla uses it to give a regiment to another title and to count how many a title owns or who controls them.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the regiments that pass these checks.

label: Parent
summary: Each of the character's parents.
details: Gives both parents. The items are characters. Vanilla often writes `even_if_dead` in the list block, which suggests dead parents are left out otherwise (inferred, the game's documentation does not say). Vanilla uses it to send messages, give opinions, and pick a guardian or a dead parent.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the parents that pass these checks.

fields.name: even_if_dead
fields.text: Vanilla writes this in the block of the random and any forms, apparently to include dead parents too (inferred, the game's documentation does not say).

label: Parent culture
summary: Each culture that the current culture came from, one step up.
details: Works on a culture. The items are cultures. A culture formed from a mix can have more than one. Vanilla uses it to test heritage and traditions of the parents.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the cultures that pass these checks.

label: Parent culture or above
summary: Each ancestor culture of the current culture, at any distance.
details: Works on a culture. It goes further than the parent culture list. Vanilla uses it to test whether a culture descends from a certain culture, such as the Greek culture, or has a certain heritage.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the cultures that pass these checks.

label: Participant group
summary: Each participant group of the situation, in all of its sub-regions.
details: Works on a situation. A participant group seems to be a set of characters taking part in the situation together (inferred from vanilla's checks for a character in a group). Vanilla uses it for movement groups in situations, to find a group by type or by member, and to favour a movement or recalculate the groups.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the groups that pass these checks.

fields.name: order_by
fields.text: Only for the ordered form: the value used to rank the groups.

label: Past holder
summary: Each earlier holder of the title, from the earliest to the latest.
details: Works on a title. The items are characters. Vanilla uses it to find the founder of a title or a particular holder, and to check nicknames.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the holders that pass these checks.

label: Past holder, newest first
summary: Each earlier holder of the title, from the latest to the earliest.
details: Works on a title. The items are characters. It is the same set as the past holder list in the opposite order, so position 0 is the most recent holder. Vanilla uses it to find the last emperor.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the holders that pass these checks.

fields.name: position
fields.text: Only for the ordered form: which rank to pick, starting at 0.

label: Patroned holy order
summary: Each holy order that the character is the patron of.
details: Works on a character. The items are holy orders. Vanilla uses it to look at the order's leader and the leader's capital or faith.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the orders that pass these checks.

label: Personally claimed artifact
summary: Each artifact that the character claims personally.
details: Works on a character. The items are artifacts. Vanilla uses it to collect claimable artifacts for transfer after a war.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the artifacts that pass these checks.

label: Personal tenet
summary: Each personal tenet of the character.
details: Works on a character. The items are tenets (the beliefs of a faith); the game's documentation only says they are the character's personal tenets. Vanilla uses it to pick or test tenets, for example whether one has a certain virtue.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the tenets that pass these checks.

fields.name: order_by
fields.text: Only for the ordered form: the value used to rank the tenets.

fields.name: position
fields.text: Only for the ordered form: which rank to pick, starting at 0.

label: Pinned character
summary: Each character that the player has pinned.
details: Works on a character, the player's. The items are characters. Vanilla uses it only to compare against another character.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the pinned characters that pass these checks.

label: Pinned province
summary: Each province that the player has pinned.
details: Works on a character. The items are provinces. The game documents nothing more, and vanilla does not use it.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the provinces that pass these checks.

label: Pinned title
summary: Each title that the player has pinned.
details: Works on a character. The items are titles. The game documents nothing more, and vanilla does not use it.

fields.name: limit
fields.text: Keeps only the titles that pass these checks.
